site.title: LIMS/ELN Program Specification
site.description: A source-bound guide to the five repositories that share the LIMS/ELN program contract.

release.label: 0.3.1 candidate
release.summary: Version 0.3.1 is the current Program candidate. It binds accepted Governance 2.1.0, Implementation 0.3.2, Simulation, and Comparison release subjects with their selected-future semantics; the authorized Program promotion route supplies the remaining Program coordinate.
release.evidenceBoundary: The pages describe the candidate at the Git commit recorded in the projection manifest. Release promotion, hosted publication, configured environments, and accountable acceptance retain their own evidence and decision paths.

program.name: Program specification
program.summary: Defines intent, shared contract content, examples, decisions, forecasts, and acceptance boundaries.
program.next: Begin here when you need the common vocabulary or the route to another authority.

actual.name: Enterprise implementation
actual.summary: Owns running code, durable behavior, infrastructure, migrations, and observed execution evidence.
actual.next: Continue here when the question depends on what the active system does.

simulation.name: Simulated final state
simulation.summary: Owns the executable selected future, its assumptions, and the results explicitly identified as simulated.
simulation.next: Continue here when you need the modeled future behavior or its explicit assumptions.

comparison.name: Comparative evidence
comparison.summary: Owns paired runs, puts their results into one comparison shape, classifies differences, and publishes readable reports.
comparison.next: Continue here when you need to understand how accepted results agree or differ.

governance.name: Site Reading governance
governance.summary: Owns shared schemas, language rules, workflows, templates, and governance rules.
governance.next: Continue here when you need a governed schema or the rule that defines a shared record.

publicRoutes.name: Golden Specimen comparison
publicRoutes.summary: Read the accepted paired report, its agreement and divergence classifications, and the evidence boundary for the selected implementation and simulation observations.

contracts.name: Repository role and release status
contracts.summary: The release-role record states what this repository owns, the candidate status, its contract links, the standing branch controls, and the release-specific review route. Only the Program release coordinate awaits promotion.

contracts.name: Constellation map
contracts.summary: The constellation record names all five repositories and the behavior each one owns.

contracts.name: Constellation lock
contracts.summary: The lock records each accepted sibling release subject and its decision-changing semantic bindings. Only the Program coordinate remains a placeholder until the authorized promotion route supplies its permanent commit and tree.

contracts.name: Program release observation
contracts.summary: The version-specific record starts with planned post-tag evidence fields and later carries the signed Program subject, hosted proof, merge admission, independent review, and GitHub review record from a separate observation commit.

contracts.name: Bounded operation catalog
contracts.summary: The packaged catalog gives implementation, simulation, and comparison work one versioned operation vocabulary.

contracts.name: Golden Specimen scenario
contracts.summary: The synthetic journey gives producers one executable scenario with a stable identity and one content digest used by every consumer.

contracts.name: Golden Specimen result schema
contracts.summary: The closed schema defines the decision-relevant result shape that both producers can project while retaining their own evidence detail.

verification.coverage: The local Pages aggregate creates two isolated sites, compares every byte, validates the complete file manifest and visitor links, and scans the generated text for credential-shaped values. Browser rendering, hosted responses, domain configuration, and publication approval remain with their fitting later observations.
